comments.body:
⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the new cycle guard truncates legitimate branch walks — silent context loss when below-window records exceed the resident set**

The rewritten guard bounds the walk by the **resident** count only:

```dart
var walked = 0;
while (current != null) {
  if (!current.timestampDegraded) path.add(current);
  if (++walked > _entries.length) break;   // ← _entries excludes _appendedBelow
  ...
  final parent = _byId[parentId] ?? _appendedBelow[parentId];
```

But the walk itself traverses `_appendedBelow` records (leaf and parent lookups both fall through to it), and those are NOT members of `_entries` (`_ingestBelowWindow` indexes them "without being indexed" into the window; same for the deep-paged append path at `windowed_session_storage.dart:1198–1201`). Any legitimate branch longer than the resident set is silently cut.

**Verified by execution** on this branch (repro: 650-record chain → `jumpToRecord('m1')` deep-pages the window → a second process appends 250 records chained from the tail → `ingestAppended()` → `getPathToRoot('x250')`):

- expected (origin/main, no guard): **250** records
- actual: **101** records — the oldest 149 ancestors of the live branch vanish from the path

This is precisely the shared-file scenario the incident describes (a second `fa` process appending to the same JSONL while this instance is deep-paged). `getPathToRoot` feeds `buildContextMessages`, so the model silently loses the oldest context of the appended region — a regression that also violates the card's own REG-1 invariant ("zero behavior change for valid input"). Note the sibling guard in `JsonlSessionStorage.getPathToRoot` (line 1914) is safe: there `_entries` holds every record and `walked ≡ path.length` for valid input.

**Fix sketch**: bound by `_entries.length + _appendedBelow.length` (still finite, admits every legitimate walk), or carry a visited-id set.

# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc63dAm3` — ⚠️ IMPORTANT: walk guard truncates below-window branches

**Fixed** in commit `0eddc5fc3` (`lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`, `getPathToRoot`), regression test in the same commit: `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` → live tail group, `gh-2178 review: a below-window branch longer than the resident set is NOT truncated by the walk guard`.

## What changed

The cycle guard now bounds by the **whole reachable union** — resident records plus the below-window appended set — instead of the resident set alone:

```dart
if (++walked > _entries.length + _appendedBelow.length) break;
```

This is exactly the review's fix sketch (still finite, still terminates an adversarial parentId cycle): the walk only ever visits records from `_byId ∪ _appendedBelow`, those two maps are disjoint (a record leaves `_appendedBelow` the moment it re-enters the window) and `_entries`/`_byId` move in lockstep, so `_entries.length + _appendedBelow.length` is exactly the union size — every legitimate (acyclic) walk fits, and a cycle still terminates after at most one pass over the union. The comment on the guard documents why the count rides the walk itself (degraded records shrink the path; the all-degraded cycle must terminate too).

## Test (TDD)

Mirrors the verified repro at fixture scale: 10-record seed, `chunkRecords: 5`, `jumpToRecord('e2')` deep-pages the window, a second process appends a 10-record chain below the window (longer than the 5-record resident set), `ingestAppended()`.

- Before the fix: `getPathToRoot('e19')` returned **6** records (`e14..e19`) — the oldest 14 ancestors silently vanished from model context (the review's 101-of-250 signature).
- After the fix: the walk resolves the full 20-record path to root (`e0..e19`) — zero truncation, REG-1 zero-drift semantics restored.

Full windowed suite green after the fix — the four affected suites (record_quarantine, session_repair, windowed storage, windowed property) run **97 tests passed** on the final tree, including the pre-existing walk/window/eviction tests.

## Automated Code Review — BLOCK

**Summary**: The gh-2178 protocol itself is sound — strict-first never-throwing `parseRecordTimestamp` (INV4 holds by construction), walk exclusion, deduped flood-capped reporting, and the repair scan all pass their 34-test suite plus the full `test/session test/providers test/env` run. Two verified defects block merge.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `_spanTextToWrite` (`session_repair.dart:691`) splices line fixes using byte offsets as UTF-16 string offsets — any multi-byte UTF-8 content in the merged span corrupts the repaired session file (verified: unparseable spliced line; the poison record becomes a permanently torn line).
- ⚠️ The new windowed walk guard (`windowed_session_storage.dart:1258`) bounds by the resident set only and ignores `_appendedBelow` — legitimate below-window branches truncate silently (verified: 250-record chain returns 101), losing model context in the incident's own shared-file scenario.

**Next Steps**:
1. Fix `_spanTextToWrite` to splice in byte space / per line; add a non-ASCII repair fixture.
2. Bound the walk by `_entries.length + _appendedBelow.length`; add a below-window-chain test.
3. Digest: no curated `## Unreleased` CHANGELOG entry (AGENTS.md:2036 convention); ticket E2E hooks (E2E-1/E2E-2) have no PR-level equivalent; `quarantineFixedLine`'s `jsonEncode` re-encodes non-ASCII payload as `\uXXXX` (byte-delta beyond the timestamp); local-vs-UTC epoch-placeholder asymmetry with `ProviderQuota`'s missing-`updatedAt` fallback.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
🚨 severity: BLOCKING —
🚨 **BLOCKING: `fa session repair` corrupts the session file when the fixed line shares a merged span with multi-byte UTF-8 content**

`_spanTextToWrite` splices gh-2178 line rewrites into a merged kept span using **byte offsets as UTF-16 code-unit offsets** on the decoded string:

```dart
final original = utf8.decode(bytes, allowMalformed: true); // code units
...
buffer.write(original.substring(cursor - span.$1, key - span.$1)); // byte offsets!
final lineEnd = original.indexOf('\n', key - span.$1);             // byte offset!
cursor = lineEnd < 0 ? span.$2 : span.$1 + lineEnd + 1;
```

`SessionScannedLine.start`/`end` are **byte** offsets (`session_line_scanner.dart:36–47`), and kept spans merge contiguous lines (`_appendSpan`), so any multi-byte UTF-8 content (non-ASCII payload — normal in this project) before the poison line inside the same merged span shifts every byte offset off the string positions.

**Verified by execution** on this branch (repro: header + a message with Russian payload `привет мир — длинная русская строка для многобайтности` + poison custom line + a child message; `repairSessionLedgers`):

```
repaired file has unparseable lines:
{"type":"custom","id":"poison-1","parentId":"m1"{"type":"custom","id":"poison-1","parentId":"m1","ti…
```

The splice cut mid-record and concatenated two half-lines — the repaired file replaces the live session file via the atomic swap, the poison record becomes a **permanently unreadable torn line** (gh-1073 conservatism keeps it verbatim on every future repair), and only `<file>.bak` remains recoverable. The PR's own tests pass only because their fixtures are pure ASCII (byte offsets ≡ char offsets). This is the sanctioned unbrick tool for exactly the incident's 664 MB Russian-language session — it must not mangle it.

**Fix sketch**: splice in byte space, or per line — split the span's raw bytes on `0x0A` (`List<int>.indexOf`), then per line emit either `utf8.decode(lineBytes)` or `lineRewrites[key]!.replacement`, never mixing byte offsets into decoded-string positions. Add a non-ASCII fixture to the repair test (e.g. a Cyrilic message line adjacent to the poison line).
